The Shining Hit Closer to Home Than I Expected
I’ve always heard about it, seen the “HERES JOHNNY” and scene with Danny rounding the corner on the tricycle and covering his eyes, but honestly was not expecting it to be as scary as it was, and frankly as fascinatingly triggering as it was. I’m a 21 year old boy, who was once a little brown floppy haired only child, largely unsocialized with no friends in an unstable home life, haunted by nightmares and general fear, with a neurotic mother I felt safe with but also unsure of, and a “only happy when he’s drunk“ alcoholic father with anger issues that I frankly was afraid of/uncomfortable with, who was also once a brown floppy haired boy haunted by an unstable home life and trauma he won’t talk about but tries to outrun. I know this sounds melodramatic, and my situation of course wasn't nearly as extreme as the film, but I genuinely can’t think of a movie that made me think about and face my trauma like this one, which is why its effectively scary/intimidating in a way that no other movie I’ve seen has been for me.

It brings all those feelings that I used to and still live with to an extent back to the surface, the underlying fear of what could be around the corner when you’re alone, “will mom or dad hurt each other?, or “will one of them hurt me by accident or on purpose?“ “was the paranormal nightmare from when I was 4-5 I still remember real or just an incredibly vivid dream?“. Like I said, I know this is dramatic, but The Shining told me to break the cycle, and overcome the darkness that may try to eat at you as effectively as any therapy session I’ve been in. I was expecting it to get creepy, but was really not expecting the feelings it gave me to be so familiar, quite impressive.

Bodhi from Point Break essentially acts as the ultimate archetype for the modern, toxic tech bro CEO.
Ok so this is one of my favorite over the top guilty pleasures. Its one of those so bad that's good films. Keanu Reeves may have totally sucked in this movie but wildly entertaining because he is, giving it his all in every scene. And Gary Busey is at his usual bonkers performance. But the late Patrick Swayze hit the nail in his portrayal of Bodhi, the ultimate Surfer dude. But for some reason, Bodhi reminds me of a tech bro, albait, much cooler version. It makes me wonder if this film was a major inspiration for every tech bro out there.

If you look past the 1991 bleach-blonde hair and the surfboards, Bodhi isn't just a surfer; he’s a disruptor running a high-stakes startup with a cult-like workplace culture. Modern tech bros don't just want to sell software; they want to "change the world" and "break the status quo." Bodhi views his bank robberies the exact same way. He explicitly tells Johnny Utah that they aren't robbing banks for the money, they are doing it to protest against a system that kills the human spirit. It is the ultimate form of pseudo-philosophical corporate branding. This film is an exercise in how the spirit of the 60's radicalism died.

Bodhi is deeply into a specific brand of spirituality, biohacking, and extreme lifestyle optimization. He treats surfing the "50-Year Storm" the way a Silicon Valley founder treats an ayahuasca retreat or a grueling ultra-marathon. It’s a performative pursuit of "enlightenment" used to justify incredibly reckless, self-serving behavior. Perhaps it just the self centered focus on living his own life free of constraints. Bodhi robbing banks does not bring the system any closer to its knees. Its not like he is out there building insurgent networks and logistical pipelines of arms for sympathizers to resist the system. Nope, for him the ultimate act of resistance is riding a super-wave, LOL.

Like a tech founder who burns through millions of venture capital dollars while protecting their own shares, Bodhi talks a big game about ultimate freedom but happily lets others pay the price. When the data starts leaking (or in his case, when the FBI closes in), he doesn't pivot safely. He doubles down, pushes his "employees" into increasingly dangerous situations, and ultimately leaves his ride-or-die team to take the fall.

Much like Steve Jobs or Elizabeth Holmes, Bodhi possesses a magnetic, cult-like charisma. He creates a "reality distortion field" where his followers willingly risk their lives and freedom because they want to be close to his vision. He says lines like "If you want the ultimate freedom, you've got to be willing to pay the ultimate price". That could easily be slapped onto a LinkedIn post about hustle culture.

Makes me want to imagine a version where Bodhi wouldn't be chasing waves in Byron Bay; he’d be living in Austin, running an unregulated crypto exchange or an AI startup, and convincing his developers to work 100-hour weeks for "the collective evolution of humanity."

Just watched Furiosa. Solid movie - but feels pretty underwhelming in comparison to Fury Road

A prequel about Furiosa is not really something I was ever particularly interested in, even with how amazing her character was in Fury Road. But I'll never say no to more Mad Max-related stuff from George Miller. I went into Furiosa with reserved expectations just because of the insanely high bar Fury Road set as one of the greatest action movies of all time. I don't want to turn this into a Fury Road glaze session (although it's hard not to) but given that this is a very directly-connected prequel with a lot of the same characters, you pretty much *have* to bring it up.

I think managing my expectations really did help a lot because Furiosa, while being a pretty well-made action movie, is nowhere near the level of Fury Road.

It's not *bad* or anything and there's a lot it does pretty well. Chris Hemsworth for example is amazing as Dementus and might in fact be my favourite villain of the entire franchise. It's such a fun performance - he really seems like he's having a blast. Tom Burke was very good as Praetorian Jack as well.

The movie also does a good job of deepening the worldbuilding from Fury Road and just...having more of an actual story.

In terms of the stunts and set pieces, while it doesn't really hit those Fury Road highs, there are some great ones here as well, especially the central War Rig sequence.

Now in terms of what doesn't work:

\- The pacing is really wonky. The first hour is honestly a bit of a slog. I know we had to see Furiosa develop from a child into a capable warrior but this sequence really dragged for me. Fury Road's pacing is just pitch-perfect - that movie doesn't have a single wasted second, which I didn't really feel with Furiosa. It just jumps from one plot point to the next without letting the story breathe. It feels both rushed *and* sluggish at the same time. It's really missing that purity of focus that Fury Road had

\- There was a lot of CG in this one, which I don't mind in a vacuum, but a lot of it honestly looked pretty bad and stuck out like a sore thumb

\- Anya Taylor-Joy does a good facsimile of Charlize Theron's Furiosa voice, but ultimately she just doesn't have the sauce to come off as a badass warrior like Charlize does, even as a young version of the character. Charlize Theron just has this *intensity* that I never really saw with ATJ. In fact, I got almost *nothing* from this character. She's almost a complete blank slate

So overall, this doesn't really hold a candle to Fury Road (which, let's be fair, very few action films do) but is still a pretty solid movie on its own merits.

Just watched Disclosure Day
I must say I was really disappointed by it. The movie was meaningless and meandering. It feels like Spielberg is out of touch with the Zeitgeist on sci-fi storytelling. He fell back in his decades-old formula and failed spectacularly on delivering on both, a compelling alien exposé and a touching personal/emotional saga.

The maddening simplicity of the details felt lazy and devoid of novelty. I kept asking myself at many points during the watching if I should change the channel and cut my losses. Spielberg sadly appears to think that he still has the same audience he had of The Close Encounter and ET. The sheer number of sci-fi movies and series on streaming services over the past 15 odd years has advanced the art of this genre far beyond that. Truly a lost opportunity by one of our generation’s best movie makers.

I would not recommend this movie even to a casual viewer. There are many better alternatives like Arrival, District 9, and Annihilation, among others to invest your time and well-earned money in.

Take on Irreplaceable You (2018 movie)
So, on a random Sunday, I came across this movie, and my decision to watch it was largely based on its poster. There was a cute girl sitting on the shoulders of a cute, clean-shaven guy with a very prominent dimple. What can I say? The poster did its job.
Going into the movie, I was expecting a deep, moving love story. Sam and Abbie had the history to make it one: childhood sweethearts who had been together for nearly two decades. But somehow, that love never quite translated onto the screen. Or maybe I just didn’t get it.
Abbie seemed determined to stay in control of Sam’s life, deciding who he should date, when he should move on, and even who would take care of him. Sam, on the other hand, seemed rather lost when it came to Abbie. He didn’t quite know how to support her or navigate what was happening between them.
And then there was Dominic, the nurse, who somehow seemed more emotionally invested in Abbie than Sam did.
By the end, Sam’s marriage proposal felt less like a declaration of love and more like an act of pity. Perhaps that wasn’t the intention, but that’s how it came across to me.
For a couple who had spent almost their entire lives together, I expected to feel their love. Unfortunately, I was left wondering whether I had missed something or whether the movie had.
Let me know what you think of it.

Children of Men (2006) was the first dystopian film I ever really watched. It was set in 2027…

I love this film for so many reasons, the detail, the very realistic take on the future and the surrounding politics. I was probably 14 when I first watched it and I have probably watched it 30 times since then.

The detail is flawless - London had only won the bid for the 2012 Olympics the year before its release and yet Theo is wearing a London 2012 Olympic jumper in the scene at Jasper’s House.

All other futuristic/dystopian films showed a world of technological advance well beyond what was realistic when you look back but not Children of Men.

I’m watching it again right now and despite the fact the fertility thing hasn’t happened it just feels so honest and not that distant.

Did anyone else love this film? I would easily put it in my top 10. Thoughts please!

2026 has been the best year for movies in more than a decade
This past weekend I saw La Bola Negra and the documentary You Can See Everything. Both great in a different way and probably contenders of best picture and directors. This year has been great in movies, of course it’s the year of the Odyssey (personally I liked it but not for best picture or director). Project Hail Mary was also a big thing. The Drama and The Invite are also personally some of my favorites. Some people love Digger and Primetime. And we still have some big contenders to release: Wild Horse Nine, The debut and Artificial. Dune Part III is also coming, even though I have not seen a lot of hype lately.
It’s been also a big year for Marvel, for Spiderman Brand New Day and Avengers Doomsday. Obsession and Backrooms were a bit hit for independent horror. Resident Evil, Other Mommy.
It’s also had some fan acclaimed movies like Coyote v Acme or The Sheep Detectives. I wasn’t fan of a lot of them like Wuthering Heights, Street Fighter, The Social Reckoning, Michael or Disclosure day, but they still have a lot of people going to the movies for. The new Godzilla or the new Hunger Games prequel.
I haven’t loved many of the animation movies but there are a lot of them this year: Super Mario Galaxy, Minions vs Monsters, Toy Story 5, Hoppers, Forgotten Island, Hexed or Wildwood.
To be honest I love to see it. I hope this makes the end of a recession and it keeps going up. More new original stories. The theaters were packed this weekend and I hope people keeps going.
